newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian non-tax payment rising-tax watchdog.
newsitem.headline: Russian non-tax payment rising-tax watchdog.

text.p: Russian company non-payment of taxes is rising and had barely been affected by attempts to use the threat of bankruptcy to increase tax collection, a State Tax Service official said on Wednesday.

Olga Samolyotova, deputy director of a Tax Service department on tax evasion, said tax debt increased to 61 trillion roubles on November 1 from 53 trillion roubles a month earlier and about 30 trillion on November 1, 1995.
Action by the Federal Bankruptcy Administration, which Russia has used since October to chase delinquent tax payers, had had only limited impact in bringing in new funds, she said.
"In relation to some firms, it played a role, but in general it did not affect the situation. The growth of tax debt continues to take place," she said.

Pyotr Mostovoi, chairman of the Federal Bankruptcy Administration, told reporters that he believed his group's efforts to use bankruptcy law to force tax debtors to pay up had had positive effects among those least inclined to pay.
He said the data was not yet conclusive without December figures.
"We don't have enough data -- it is only complete for October -- to show the trend," said Mostovoi.
But he said the Administration was not attacking many large tax debtors, because it was designed to investigate only companies which were not able to pay their taxes.
"Our measures, arising from (bankruptcy) law, are oriented towards those organisations which, legally speaking, are bankrupt firms -- not able to pay. And those (larger) debtors are able to pay."
Such companies capable of paying their taxes would be targeted by other government agencies, he said.
